guid-typescript.note: The npm package and its repository (https://github.com/NicolasDeveloper/guid-typescript, read 2026-10-09) carry no licence file; the ISC licence is declared in package.json only. The code is inlined in the onnxruntime-web bundle.

pip:certifi.evidence: Metadata gives only the classifier 'Mozilla Public License 2.0 (MPL 2.0)'; the LICENSE file is the MPL-2.0 notice for the bundled CA certificate list.

pip:psycopg2-binary.evidence: Metadata says 'LGPL with exceptions'; the LICENSE file grants the GNU LGPL version 3 or later, plus a linking exception for OpenSSL.

pip:python-dateutil.evidence: Metadata says 'Dual License'; the LICENSE file offers the Apache License 2.0 or the BSD 3-clause licence (code before December 2017 is BSD-3-Clause only).

npm:axe-core.reason: MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft. The package is only loaded by the accessibility checks of the end-to-end suite (frontend/e2e/app/a11y.spec.ts); it is not in the production bundle (verified from the build's source maps), is used unmodified and is not redistributed.

npm:@axe-core/playwright.reason: MPL-2.0, same as axe-core: test tooling only, unmodified, not in the production bundle, not redistributed.

npm:caniuse-lite.reason: Data licensed CC-BY-4.0 (attribution), read by Babel/browserslist while building. Nothing of it is in the production bundle (verified from the build's source maps) or in any image, so no attribution obligation arises from distribution; dropping it is not possible without dropping the Vite React plugin.

pip:certifi.reason: MPL-2.0 covers only the CA certificate list, which is data. It is installed unmodified from PyPI (a dependency of requests), so the MPL source-availability duty is met by PyPI and the upstream repository; copyleft does not reach Doory's code.

pip:psycopg2-binary.reason: LGPL-3.0-or-later (with an OpenSSL linking exception), the PostgreSQL driver Django uses. It stays a separate library: installed unmodified from PyPI by pip, imported dynamically, never vendored or patched, so Doory itself remains MIT; an operator can replace it with another build (pip install). psycopg 3 is LGPL-3.0 too and Django has no permissive PostgreSQL driver, so a swap would not help. Condition: never copy its code into this repository.

pip:hypothesis.reason: MPL-2.0, used unmodified by the property-based tests. It is only in requirements-dev.txt, which the Dockerfile does not install, so it is neither in the image nor redistributed.

pip:pillow.reason: The wheel's LICENSE (MIT-CMU for Pillow) also reproduces the notices of the libraries bundled in the wheel; FreeType is offered under the FreeType Licence or the GPL-2.0 and the FreeType Licence applies. The GPL text is not what Pillow is distributed under.

pip:botocore.reason: The NOTICE lists the vendored requests (Apache-2.0) and urllib3 (MIT) and Mozilla's CA bundle, which is MPL-2.0 data. botocore itself is Apache-2.0.

purposes.npm:@fontsource-variable/caveat: UI handwriting font (variable Caveat) for notes and captions, served by the app: woff2 files in the bundle
purposes.npm:@fontsource-variable/fraunces: UI display font (variable Fraunces, with the optical-size axis) for headings and the wordmark, served by the app: woff2 files in the bundle
purposes.npm:@fontsource-variable/inter: default body font of text in designs (variable Inter), bundled so new text renders instantly and offline: woff2 files in the bundle
purposes.npm:@fontsource-variable/nunito: UI body font (variable Nunito), served by the app: woff2 files in the bundle
purposes.npm:@fontsource-variable/plus-jakarta-sa: default heading font of text in designs (variable Plus Jakarta Sans), bundled so new text renders instantly and offline: woff2 files in the bundle
purposes.npm:@tanstack/react-query: server-state cache of the app shell
purposes.npm:fflate: ZIP archive of a multi-page image export (lazy-loaded; also a dependency of jspdf)
purposes.npm:gifenc: colour reduction (PnnQuant) and LZW compression of the animated GIF export (lazy-loaded, 11 kB minified). Dithering and removal of repeated frames are Doory's own (`frontend/src/editor/engine/export/video/gifPixels.ts`)
purposes.npm:lib0: binary encoding helpers used by the Yjs protocols
purposes.npm:mp4box: reads the video clips of a design (MP4 boxes and samples) so the video export can decode each frame with WebCodecs (lazy-loaded with the export)
purposes.npm:mp4-muxer: writes the MP4 file of the video export from WebCodecs output (lazy-loaded, 9 kB gzipped). Its author has deprecated it in favour of Mediabunny, which is MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft) and so outside the permissive list; 5.2 does what the export needs
purposes.npm:onnxruntime-web: in-browser model runtime for background removal: the WebAssembly CPU build, loaded lazily and run in a Web Worker (the `.wasm` file is built by Microsoft from onnxruntime and its third-party sources, see the notes below)
purposes.npm:webm-muxer: writes the WebM file of the video export (lazy-loaded, 7 kB gzipped); same deprecation note as `mp4-muxer`
purposes.npm:y-protocols: Yjs sync and awareness wire protocol
purposes.npm:@axe-core/playwright: automated accessibility checks of every shell page in the end-to-end suite (`frontend/e2e/app/a11y.spec.ts`); never part of the app bundle
purposes.npm:@vitejs/plugin-react: React support of the Vite build
purposes.npm:canvas: node-canvas for unit tests in jsdom
purposes.pip:boto3: S3-compatible object storage client (used when `USE_S3` is set)
purposes.pip:brotli: Brotli codec that fontTools needs to read and write woff2 fonts
purposes.pip:channels: ASGI and WebSocket layer of real-time co-editing
purposes.pip:channels-redis: shared channel layer for several real-time workers (with `redis-py`, MIT)
purposes.pip:defusedxml: safe XML parsing in the SVG sanitiser, element import and print layout
purposes.pip:django-unfold: theme of the Django admin used for content
purposes.pip:drf-spectacular: OpenAPI schema and the staff-only Swagger page
purposes.pip:fonttools: inspects uploaded and downloaded font files
purposes.pip:gunicorn: production WSGI server of the API
purposes.pip:pillow: validates uploaded raster images and makes thumbnails (the wheel bundles libjpeg-turbo, libpng, zlib, FreeType, HarfBuzz, LittleCMS, OpenJPEG, libwebp, libtiff; their notices are in the wheel)
purposes.pip:playwright: drives headless Chromium for server-side print PDF export. The wheel bundles Playwright's Node.js driver (MIT; its dependencies' notices are in `driver/package/ThirdPartyNotices.txt`); the browser itself is downloaded by `playwright install` only when `INSTALL_CHROMIUM=true`, see the decisions above
purposes.pip:psycopg2-binary: PostgreSQL driver of Django (the wheel bundles libpq, PostgreSQL licence, and OpenSSL, Apache-2.0)
purposes.pip:pycrdt: Yjs-compatible CRDT, bindings to the Rust `yrs` engine (real-time co-editing)
purposes.pip:pypdf: writes the TrimBox/BleedBox, `/Lang` and `/Creator` of the PDF Chromium printed; page content is copied unchanged
purposes.pip:requests: outbound HTTP: font, element pack, model and audio pack downloads, stock photo search
purposes.pip:uvicorn: production ASGI server of the real-time service
purposes.pip:websockets: WebSocket protocol implementation used by uvicorn
purposes.pip:daphne: ASGI development server (not installed in the production image)
purposes.pip:hypothesis: property-based tests; never installed in the production image or redistributed with the product
purposes.npm:axe-core: the accessibility rule engine that `@axe-core/playwright` runs in the page under test; never part of the app bundle
